content:
We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically to the given molecule (target) reproduces the forward reaction: aromatic amine attacks phenylsulfonyl chloride, forming sulfonamide, breaking S-Cl bond, forming N-S bond. So retrosynthetic step: break N-S bond to give aromatic amine and phenylsulfonyl chloride (or maybe phenylsulfonyl chloride plus amine). The target molecule is given: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O. That's a sulfonamide: sulfonyl attached to N of an aniline (aryl amine) that is further substituted with a piperazine etc. Also sulfonyl attached to a phenyl with F. So we need a template that breaks N-S bond and forms S-Cl bond (i.e., reverse of forward). So functional groups formed: sulfonamide (N-S). Broken: S-Cl. So we can search template catalog with criteria: functional_groups_formed includes "sulfonamides"? Actually functional groups formed in forward reaction: sulfonamides. So broken: "alkyl halide"? but S-Cl is a sulfonyl chloride (acyl chloride type). The functional group broken is "acyl chloride"? The list includes "acyl chloride". That is appropriate. So we search with functional_groups_formed=["sulfonamides"], functional_groups_broken=["acyl chloride"] maybe also "aryl halide"? but S-Cl is not aryl halide. Use functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"], functional_groups_broken ["acyl chloride"].

Let's call search_template_catalog_by_criteria.
